title: Logistics Control Tower
summary: A live dispatch control tower that replaced fourteen spreadsheets with one operational view across three countries.
challenge: Fourteen spreadsheets, three country teams and no shared definition of a dispatched job. The partner's client could not say how many vehicles were actually on the road at 6am.
approach: We modelled the dispatch domain first, then replaced the spreadsheets one workflow at a time, with a live board reading from the systems of record that already existed.
result: Dispatch decisions are 38% faster and the daily 6am reconciliation meeting no longer exists.
coverAlt: Dispatch control tower dashboard with live job counts, fleet utilisation and route coverage

title: Field Ops Mobile
partnerType: Product pod for a SaaS platform
summary: Offline-first job management for 900 field engineers, syncing work orders from basements and rural sites alike.
challenge: Crews worked in basements, plant rooms and rural sites where connectivity was a rumour. Every work-order app the partner had tried lost data on reconnect.
approach: Offline-first architecture: a local queue, deterministic conflict resolution, and sync states crews could read without training.
result: 4.8/5 crew satisfaction and no lost work orders since rollout.
coverAlt: Field engineer app showing today's jobs, offline sync status and a start-job action

title: Checkout Replatform
partnerType: Campaign build with a marketing agency
summary: A headless checkout and campaign microsite rebuild that held its latency budget through the busiest week of the year.
challenge: The checkout fell over every peak season, and the agency's campaign calendar could not slip to accommodate a rewrite.
approach: A headless checkout behind a feature flag, load-tested against last year's peak curve and cut over in stages outside campaign windows.
result: +21% checkout completion and a latency budget that held through peak week.
coverAlt: Headless checkout page with payment fields, order summary and a peak-latency budget

title: Claims Triage Assistant
partnerType: Data pod for an insurtech product
summary: Document classification and routing that hands claims handlers a ranked queue instead of a shared inbox.
challenge: Claims arrived in a shared inbox and were triaged by whoever opened it first. The partner needed throughput without hiring more handlers.
approach: Document classification feeding a ranked routing queue, with a human review path and an audit trail behind every automatic decision.
result: 62% less manual triage, with the same team clearing a larger volume.
coverAlt: Claims triage queue with confidence scores, extracted document fields and an audit trail

title: Plant Telemetry Migration
partnerType: Execution team for a DevOps consultancy
summary: Moved a factory telemetry platform from owned servers to containers with no production downtime.
challenge: Telemetry for a working factory ran on owned servers nobody wanted to touch, and any downtime meant stopping the line.
approach: A rehearsal in a mirrored environment, a dual-write period, and a rollback path tested before the real cutover.
result: Zero production downtime during migration and 99.97% uptime since.
coverAlt: Before-and-after diagram of factory telemetry moving from owned servers to containers

title: Patient Self-Service Portal
partnerType: Engineering partner to a design studio
summary: Appointment, results and billing self-service for 140,000 patients, built to WCAG 2.2 AA from the studio's designs.
challenge: 140,000 patients were served through a phone line, and the studio's designs carried accessibility states the previous developer had ignored.
approach: A server-rendered build to the studio's designs, WCAG 2.2 AA from the first component, tested with screen readers and keyboard-only paths.
result: 31% fewer phone contacts in the first quarter, plus an AA audit the studio could hand to its client.
coverAlt: Patient portal with next appointment, recent results, billing and an accessibility notice

title: Fleet Telemetry Pipeline
partnerType: Overflow squad for a software house
summary: Streaming telemetry that flags maintenance risk before a vehicle leaves the depot.
challenge: The partner's client only learned about a vehicle fault once it was back in the depot, usually off the road for a day.
approach: Streaming ingest from on-board units, threshold and trend models, and alerting inside the depot's own dashboard.
result: 19% lower unplanned downtime across the fleet.
coverAlt: Fleet map with live vehicle alerts, a fault prediction chart and alert rules

title: Multi-Product Design System
partnerType: Front-end build for a UX studio
summary: A token-driven component library and documentation site shared by four product squads.
challenge: Four product squads had four button components, four spacing scales and four opinions. The studio kept redesigning the same screens.
approach: A token layer first, then a component library published with usage documentation and codemods for screens that already shipped.
result: 40% faster UI delivery and one shared vocabulary across four products.
coverAlt: Design system page with colour tokens, type scale, component states and library entries

title: Payroll Integration Layer
partnerType: Integration work with a growth agency
summary: An integration layer joining payroll to twenty provider APIs with retries, audit trails and reconciliation.
challenge: Payroll had to talk to twenty provider APIs, each with its own retry behaviour, and reconciliation lived in a manual spreadsheet.
approach: A queue-based integration layer with idempotent jobs, a written contract per provider, and an audit trail for every run.
result: 99.4% reconciliation accuracy, with the manual spreadsheet retired.
coverAlt: Integration diagram linking HRIS, payroll, providers and ledger through one layer
